`GT` call signature:

```python
GT(df,                                   # the data
   caption=..., ratio_cols=..., ...,     # TableSpec: the DOCUMENT (formatted values, structure)
   style=HouseStyle(...),                # HouseStyle: the PAGE (how it is drawn)
   config_path=..., mimes=...)           # GT's own: defaults file, Jupyter bundle
```

## Arguments

**`TableSpec` — the document.** Raw data in, formatted values and structure
out: column meaning, number formats, alignment, totals, hierarchy. Each is a
`GT` keyword, or a field of a `TableSpec` passed to `build`. Every field here
changes the document and so its hash.

| Group | Fields |
|---|---|
| metadata | `caption`, `label`, `notes` |
| column meaning | `ratio_cols`, `year_cols`, `date_cols`, `raw_cols`, `html_cols`, `unbreakable` |
| column format | `formatters`, `float_format`, `int_format`, `ratio_format`, `date_format`, `table_float_format` |
| engineering notation | `pef_lower`, `pef_upper`, `eng_digits`, `eng_style` |
| alignment | `aligners` |
| rows | `row_flags`, `cell_flags`, `max_rows` |
| structure | `show_index`, `header_row`, `sparsify`, `sparsify_columns` |
| for clients | `include_raw` |

**`HouseStyle` — the page.** Rulings, widths, TikZ geometry: how one document
is drawn. A house matter, set once for a document or a site, which is why it
is called style. Never a bare keyword: always
`style=HouseStyle(...)`. Nothing here enters the document. For HTML, the rule
weights and the two widths also exist as CSS custom properties on `.gt`, and CSS
wins; the TikZ fields are TikZ only.

| Group | Fields |
|---|---|
| break line rules | `max_rule_depth`, `max_vrule_depth` |
| rule weights | `frame_rule`, `head_rule`, `stub_rule`, `total_rule`, `spanner_rule`, `hrule_widths`, `vrule_widths` |
| widths | `max_table_width_em`, `max_prose_width_em` |
| TikZ geometry and container | `tikz_scale`, `tikz_column_sep`, `tikz_row_sep`, `tikz_container_env`, `tikz_latex`, `tikz_post_process` |
| text renderer | `text_ascii_rules` |

**`GT`'s internals — neither.** Two keywords about the call, plus `style` above:

| Keyword | Does |
|---|---|
| `config_path` | load `TableSpec` defaults from a YAML file; explicit keywords override it |
| `mimes` | pin what `_repr_mimebundle_` publishes, for a target GT cannot detect (`gfm`) |

The split is the pipeline: raw data, then formatted values, then printed table. The
document is the middle term, formatted text per cell plus alignment, spans,
break depths and flags, and `TableSpec` owns everything up to it. `HouseStyle`
owns everything after. Alignment is in the document, so it is spec. The
mechanical test, when a case feels fuzzy: a spec change changes `gt.doc.hash`;
a style change never does. A style field passed as a bare keyword warns (with
the fix). Anything else unknown warns and is ignored, which allows a 5.3 call
to keep working until it is cleaned up.

## The pipeline

```text
df  ──► build(df, spec)
    ──► TableDoc   # IR
    ──► render_html / render_tikz / render_text(doc, style)
    ──► output
```

`GT(df, **spec_fields, style=...)` does both, lazily, and caches each rendering:

```python
gt = GT(df, caption='Exhibit 1', ratio_cols=['lr'], style=HouseStyle(max_table_width_em=41))
gt.doc      # the TableDoc: what the table is, hashable, JSON-serializable
gt.html     # fragment with its stylesheet
gt.tikz     # table environment + tikzpicture
gt.text     # monospace; also print(gt) and repr(gt)
gt          # in Jupyter or Quarto: the right bundle for the target
```

The document never specifies a width, a weight or a font; the renderers decide
those.

## GT70 vs GT53

| Effect | 5.3 | 7.0 |
|------|-------|-----------|
| a caption and a Quarto cross-reference | `GT(df, caption=, label=)` | the same |
| footnotes under the table | — | `notes=['Amounts in USD thousands.']` |
| hide or show the index | `show_index=False` | `show_index=False`. Default `None` hides a trivial unnamed `RangeIndex` and shows everything else |
| ratio columns as percent | `ratio_cols=['lr']` | the same, or a regex: `ratio_cols='lr\|ratio$'` |
| years without commas | `year_cols=['year']` | the same |
| two decimals on one column | `formatters={'paid': 2}` gives `1234.57` | `formatters={'paid': 2}` gives `1,234.57`. An int groups now. Write `'.2f'` for ungrouped |
| a format string on one column | `formatters={'x': '{x:.1%}'}` | the same, and the short form `',.1f'` works too |
| every float the same way | `default_float_str='{x:,.3f}'` | `float_format=',.3f'`. Turns float inference off, including the engineering switch |
| integers, ratios, dates work the same way | `default_integer_str`, `default_ratio_str`, `default_date_str` | `int_format`, `ratio_format`, `date_format` |
| quick look at everything at 6 dp | `table_float_format` | the same, and it still beats a `formatters` entry. Call site only, never a config file |
| alignment | `aligners='lrr'` | the same, or `aligners={'paid': 'r'}` |
| a column that must not wrap | `unbreakable=['id']` | the same |
| a total row | by hand, after the fact | `row_flags={-1: ['total']}`. Also `subtotal`, `emphasis`, `muted`, by position or callable |
| more than 50 rows without an error | `large_ok=True` | nothing: 7.0 truncates at 200 with a note. `max_rows=None` for everything |
| rules between row groups | `hrule_widths=(1, 0.5, 0)` | `style=HouseStyle(max_rule_depth='auto')` picks the depths; `hrule_widths` the weights. See below |
| verticals between column groups | `vrule_widths=(1, 0, 0)` | `style=HouseStyle(max_vrule_depth=1, vrule_widths=...)`. Needs a MultiIndex on the columns |
| the PDF table is too wide | `tikz_scale=0.8` | `style=HouseStyle(max_table_width_em=41, tikz_scale=0.9)`. Budget first, scale is a ceiling. See below |
| one prose column is too wide | `max_str_length=40` | `style=HouseStyle(max_prose_width_em=18)`. Wraps, never truncates |
| one set of house rules for a document | `config_path='house.yaml'` | the same, or `partial(GT, config_path='house.yaml')` |
| a `quarto render --to gfm` build | — | `GT(df, mimes=('text/plain',))`. The only target GT cannot detect |

: How to achieve various effects in GT. {#tbl-a}

Anything not here is on the complete map in the [migration page](https://greater-tables-project.readthedocs.io/en/latest/migration.html).

**Notes.**

**Rule depth.** A row's *break depth* is the shallowest index level whose value changed. `'auto'`
rules every break except the innermost level, so a two-level index gets a rule where the outer
value changes and nothing else, and a flat index gets no internal rules at all. An int is literal:
`max_rule_depth=0` on a flat index rules every row whose stub changed. `None` draws none.
`max_vrule_depth` is the same idea for column groups.

**Width.** `max_table_width_em` is a target, not a guarantee, and it is `None` unless you set it:
a bare `GT(df)` in a PDF gets natural widths. With a budget, TikZ narrows the wrapping columns
first, all by the same quantile so each carries the same chance of wrapping, and columns that must
not wrap hold their width. Only when the floors alone exceed the budget does it step `tikz_scale`
down a fixed ladder and logs a warning. `tikz_scale` is the largest scale it may use,
not the size it will use. At 11pt, 455pt of text block is about 41em. HTML hands the number to the
browser as a CSS `max-width` and lets it measure.

**Math and dollars.** `$...$` is math anywhere text appears. Delimiters must be tight against
their content, a span may not contain another `$`, and a closing `$` may not be followed by a
digit, so `$10 to $20` is two prices and `$\psi(u)$` is math. Nothing to configure. Write `\$` for
a literal dollar next to a real span.

## Common idioms

Column selectors are regexes searched against the column name, so anchor one that could match
inside a longer name. Format sugar is lowercase and has no width field: `'.3e'`, not `'7.3E'`.

```python
from functools import partial
from greater_tables import GT, HouseStyle

# columns LR, CR, ER as 0.0% (ratio columns already default to one decimal)
GT(df, ratio_cols=r'^[LCE]R$', ratio_format='.1%')

# every untagged float column at ,.2f, beating any formatters entry
GT(df, table_float_format=',.2f')

# all floats in scientific notation, three decimals: 3.123e+10
GT(df, float_format='.3e')                  # uppercase E is not parsed; see pending

# all numbers to one significant figure: 1e+03, 0.002
GT(df, float_format='.1g', int_format='.1g')

# one named column through my own function; it owns NaN handling and
# does not reach the document, so a client cannot re-render that column
GT(df, formatters={'paid': my_format})

# overall width target, in ems; 41em is an A4 text block at 11pt
GT(df, style=HouseStyle(max_table_width_em=41))

# columns A and B never wrap
GT(df, unbreakable=['A', 'B'])

# width budget and a scale ceiling together: at most 0.9, less if it must
GT(df, style=HouseStyle(max_table_width_em=41, tikz_scale=0.9))

# rule weights by depth slot: 0 none, 0.25 ultra thin ... 1 semithick, 3 ultra thick
GT(df, style=HouseStyle(hrule_widths=(1, 0.5, 0.25), vrule_widths=(0.5, 0.25, 0.25)))

# a document-wide GT with its house rules baked in
house_GT = partial(GT, ratio_cols=r'^[LCE]R$', year_cols=r'^(year|ay)$',
                   style=HouseStyle(max_table_width_em=41, tikz_scale=0.9))
```

GT does not guess a column's meaning from its name. csv-viewer does (`year`, `id`, money and
percent words in the header), because it has only a header to go on; GT has the dtype and the
values, and a publication table wants the tag stated. The `partial` above is the way to state it
once.

## Cell format rules

A cell's format is decided per column, in three steps. The decision is never per cell: always one column, one format.

**1. Kind.** The column's semantic tag if it has one, else its dtype. Tags come from the
selectors; when more than one matches, the first of `ratio`, `year`, `date`, `raw` wins. An
**untagged** column is one no selector matched, so its dtype decides: `int`, `float`, `date`,
`datetime`, or string and everything else. "Untagged float" is a float column that is not a
ratio, a year, a date or raw, which is most of them.

**2. Format.** For that kind, the first thing that is set, reading left to right:

| Kind | first | then | then | finally |
|------|---------|---------|--------|------|
| ratio | `formatters[col]` | `ratio_format` | percent, one decimal | |
| year | `formatters[col]` | plain integer, no grouping | | |
| date tag, or date dtype | `formatters[col]` | `date_format` | ISO date | |
| datetime dtype | `formatters[col]` | `date_format` | ISO date and time to the minute | |
| raw | `formatters[col]` | `str(value)` | | |
| int | `formatters[col]` | `int_format` | grouped integer | |
| **untagged float** | **`table_float_format`** | `formatters[col]` | `float_format` | inferred, step 3 |
| string, bool, other | `formatters[col]` | `str(value)` | | |

Two things to notice. A per-column `formatters` entry beats a house default on every line but
one: `table_float_format` is above it on the untagged-float line, and nowhere else, which is why
it is a call-site sledgehammer and never a config entry. And `year` ignores `int_format`, since a
year has its own kind.

A `formatters` key matches the column label, or for a MultiIndex column its leaf name. A callable
entry is applied as is: it owns NaN handling, and its column carries no `FormatSpec` in the
document, so a client cannot re-render it.

**3. Inference.** Untagged floats only, and only when nothing above is set. Setting `float_format`
turns this off for the document, which is what makes twelve exhibits agree.

- Engineering notation when the mean magnitude falls outside `[10**pef_lower, 10**pef_upper]`,
  default `[0.001, 1e6]`, or when the nonzero values span more than `10**pef_upper` between
  largest and smallest. Drawn with `eng_digits` decimals in `eng_style`: `'si'` suffixes (k, M,
  µ) or `'exp'` aligned exponents.
- Otherwise decimals by mean magnitude: 5 below 1, 3 below 10, 2 below 20,000, else 0,
  grouped. The first bucket is why an untagged column of fractions prints `0.76400`: tag it
  `ratio`, or state `float_format`.

Independent of all three: a null prints as the format's `null` (an em dash); a negative value
stamps the `neg` flag from the value, not the text; and alignment is `aligners[col]` if given,
else numbers right, dates centered, text left.

### Format strings

Every format field takes the same input: a `formatters` value, `float_format`, `int_format`,
`ratio_format`, `date_format` and `table_float_format`. Each form resolves to one `FormatSpec`,
which is what the document stores.

| Form | Example | Notes |
|--------|---------------|-------------------------|
| short string | `',.2f'` | `[,][.N]T`: optional grouping comma, optional digits, one type letter |
| f-string | `'{x:,.2f}'` | the 5.3 form, same grammar inside the braces |
| int | `2` | `N` decimals, grouped: the same as `',.2f'` |
| word | `'year'`, `'eng'`, `'si'` | named kinds, below |
| date pattern | `'%d %b %Y'` | any string containing `%` that is not a number format |
| mapping | `{'kind': 'dec', 'digits': 1}` | the `FormatSpec` fields; the YAML form |
| callable | `my_format` | `formatters` only |

**Numbers.** The type letter picks the kind, and `N` means decimals except under `g`. Examples on
1234567.891 and 0.0012345:

| `T` | Kind | `N` means | Default `N` | Example | 1234567.891 | 0.0012345 |
|---|---|------|---|----|-----|-----|
| `f` | dec | decimals | 2 | `',.2f'` | 1,234,567.89 | 0.00 |
| `d` | int | ignored | | `',d'` | 1,234,568 | 0 |
| `%` | pct | decimals after ×100 | 1 | `'.1%'` | 123456789.1% | 0.1% |
| `e` | sci | mantissa decimals | 2 | `'.3e'` | 1.235e+06 | 1.234e-03 |
| `g` | gen | significant figures | 6 | `'.3g'` | 1.23e+06 | 0.00123 |
| `s` | str | ignored | | `'s'` | 1234567.891 | 0.0012345 |
| | year | | | `'year'` | 1234567 | 0 |
| | eng | mantissa decimals | 3 | `'eng'` | 1.235e+06 | 1.234e-03 |
| | si | mantissa decimals | 3 | `'si'` | 1.235M | 1.234m |

- `eng` puts the mantissa in [1, 1000) with an exponent that is a multiple of 3, written
  `e+00` so a column aligns. `si` uses the SI letters instead, from q (10^-30^) to Q (10^30^),
  with a no-break space in the empty slot so the decimal points align.
- The comma groups thousands. On `e` it is accepted and does nothing.
- A kind can cross dtypes: `formatters={'count': '.2f'}` on an integer column prints `1234.00`.
- Not accepted, and each raises at build: a width (`'10.2f'`), a sign (`'+.2f'`), fill or
  alignment (`'>10'`), `_` grouping, uppercase `E`, `F` or `G` (pending), text around the braces
  (`'{x:.2f} USD'`), a variable other than `x`, and `'{x:s}'`. For a unit or a currency symbol, use
  the mapping form's `prefix` and `suffix`.
- Two f-string forms differ from Python: `'{x:,}'` and `'{x:}'` give two decimals, not the full
  value.

**The mapping form** is the only route to parentheses, scaling, a prefix or suffix, and the
null and zero text. It is also the form a YAML config file uses.

| Field | Default | Does |
|------|------|-----------------------|
| `kind` | required | `int`, `dec`, `pct`, `sci`, `gen`, `eng`, `si`, `year`, `date` or `str` |
| `digits` | by kind | `N` above |
| `group` | `False` | thousands separators |
| `scale` | `1.0` | multiplies before formatting: `0.001` for thousands |
| `prefix`, `suffix` | none | text around the number, inside any parentheses |
| `negative` | `'minus'` | `'paren'` prints `(1,234.50)` |
| `null` | `'—'` | text for a missing value, NaN or infinity |
| `zero` | none | text for an exact zero, such as `'-'` |
| `pattern` | none | the date pattern, for kind `date` |

```python
formatters={
    'paid': {'kind': 'dec', 'digits': 2, 'group': True,
             'prefix': '$', 'negative': 'paren'},
    'premium': {'kind': 'dec', 'digits': 1, 'group': True,
                'scale': 0.001, 'suffix': 'k'}}
# paid: $1,234,567.89 and ($1,234.50); premium: 1,234.6k
```

```yaml
formatters:
  paid: {kind: dec, digits: 2, group: true, prefix: $, negative: paren}
```

Put `negative: paren` with a prefix: without it a negative prints `$-1,234.50`.

**Dates and times.** A date pattern goes to pandas `Timestamp.strftime`, so it covers the date
dtype, the datetime dtype and a `date_cols` column of strings that parse as dates. The defaults
are `'%Y-%m-%d'` for a date and `'%Y-%m-%d %H:%M'` for a datetime. `date_format` covers both, so
`'%d %b %Y'` drops the time from a datetime column. Examples on 2026-03-07 09:05:03.25:

| Code | Means | Example |
|-----|-------------------|-------------|
| `%Y`, `%y` | year, four and two digits | 2026, 26 |
| `%m` | month, 01 to 12 | 03 |
| `%b`, `%B` | month name, short and full | Mar, March |
| `%d` | day, 01 to 31 | 07 |
| `%e` | day, space padded | 7 with a leading space |
| `%#d` | day, unpadded, Windows only | 7 |
| `%-d` | day, unpadded, Linux and macOS only | fails on Windows |
| `%a`, `%A` | weekday name, short and full | Sat, Saturday |
| `%u`, `%w` | weekday number, Monday 1 and Sunday 0 | 6, 6 |
| `%j` | day of the year | 066 |
| `%U`, `%W` | week of the year, weeks starting Sunday and Monday | 09, 09 |
| `%G`, `%V` | ISO year and ISO week | 2026, 10 |
| `%H`, `%I` | hour, 24-hour and 12-hour | 09, 09 |
| `%M`, `%S` | minute, second | 05, 03 |
| `%f` | microseconds, always six digits | 250000 |
| `%p` | AM or PM | AM |
| `%z`, `%Z` | UTC offset, time zone name | empty for a naive timestamp |
| `%c`, `%x`, `%X` | locale date and time, date, time | Sat Mar 7 09:05:03 2026, 03/07/26, 09:05:03 |
| `%%` | a literal percent sign | % |

| Pattern | Example |
|-----------|-------------|
| `'%Y-%m-%d'` | 2026-03-07 |
| `'%Y-%m-%d %H:%M'` | 2026-03-07 09:05 |
| `'%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S'` | 2026-03-07T09:05:03 |
| `'%d %b %Y'` | 07 Mar 2026 |
| `'%B %d, %Y'` | March 07, 2026 |
| `'%b %Y'` | Mar 2026 |
| `'%Y-%m'` | 2026-03 |
| `'%H:%M:%S'` | 09:05:03 |
| `'%I:%M %p'` | 09:05 AM |
| `'%G-W%V'` | 2026-W10 |

- There is no quarter code: `%q` fails.
- A date pattern is recognized by its `%`, which makes two traps. The C form `'%.2f'` is taken as
  a date pattern and fails at render with "Invalid format string". A typo such as `'.2%f'` prints
  nonsense without an error.
- `'YY-mm-DD'` is not a pattern and raises. Write `'%y-%m-%d'`.

## Generating Test Cases

Generate a raw test dataframe.

```{python}
from greater_tables import GT, HouseStyle, Fabricator
from IPython.display import display
fab = Fabricator()
df = fab.make(4, 'fids12')
df
```

Basic output, defaults.

```{python}
GT(df, caption='Exhibit 1: float, integer, date, string 3 words')
```

Specify float, date, and integer formats.

```{python}
GT(df, caption='Exhibit 2',
       float_format='.4f',
       # int_format=',d',  # comma is the default
       date_format='%Y-%m-%d'
  )
```

or

```{python}
GT(df, caption='Exhibit 2',
       float_format=',.2f',
       int_format='d',  # remove comma
       date_format='%X' # %x date, %X time is handy; '%Y-%m-%d; '%H:%M:%S'
  )
```

Define a custom formatter - here to get fractions of a second

```{python}
import pandas as pd
def ms(x):
    return '—' if pd.isna(x) else x.strftime('%H:%M:%S.%f')[:-3]
time_col = df.columns[2]
GT(df, formatters={time_col: ms})
# list(map(ms, df[time_col]))
```
